study: Drummond et al. 2020, Children's Literacy Initiative (CLI) i3 Scale-Up (AIR)
eval_evidence: Evaluation conducted/authored by American Institutes for Research (AIR); CLI (the program developer/nonprofit) delivered the intervention but AIR ran the impact study.
developer_evidence: CLI, a nonprofit, 'provides teachers ... resources ... directly from CLI', including training seminars and coaching; CLI staff/coaches delivered the PD to treatment teachers.
cascade_evidence: Mixed: CLI coaches train teachers directly, but a core second component has CLI select and train Instructional Lead Teachers (ILTs) per school 'to serve as mentors' to colleagues -> a train-the-trainer/lead-teacher hop, so coded cascade.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools 'continue with business-as-usual' literacy instruction; each received only a $1,500-$2,000/yr book-purchase stipend (no active alternative PD program).
coaching_evidence: Intervention includes ~105 hours of literacy coaching per year (classroom-embedded), well above occasional; recurring in-class coaching is a core CLI component (Table 4).
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes K-3 teachers' literacy instruction (training/coaching/books); no tutoring, pull-out, or direct student-facing software dose beyond regular instruction.
maturity_evidence: Primary extracted wave = Year 3 (2018-19) of a 3-year program; teachers had >=1 prior implementation year. (Year-1 results reported but null.)
